text:
devon: heads up — I just found a `.env` uploaded in a partner CI artifact that contains a VAULT_DEV_TOKEN (short-lived but still plaintext). link: https://partner-storage.internal/ci/12345 :grimacing:
maya: ugh. how long was the token valid for?
devon: token TTL was 12h, issued yesterday morning. looks like the token scope is limited to `secret/data/dev/*` but still. artifact retention was 30d so could be crawled.
alex: can you paste a redacted snippet of the file? we need to confirm there are no DB creds or other keys.
devon: snippet (redacted):
```
# .env
VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.redwood.local
VAULT_TOKEN=s.XXXXXXREDACTEDXXXXXX
LOCAL_DB=postgres://user:***@localhost:5432/dev
```
isabel: good catch. I want to know if audit logging was enabled for that Vault namespace — if not, we should assume someone could have read the token after the artifact was created.
maya: checking Vault audit status now. one sec.
maya: vault audit backends: sys/audit/ file disabled for `dev` namespace, only `global` has audit forwarder. so per-namespace audit was not capturing reads.
samir: action items: 1) revoke the token immediately, 2) rotate any secrets accessible by that token if they are high-risk, 3) enable audit for dev namespace, 4) purge artifact and update CI to stop uploading env files.
devon: already deleted the artifact and asked partner to block access. timestamp: 1768123500.
isabel: revoke command (run as svc-vault-admin):
```
vault token revoke s.XXXXXXREDACTEDXXXXXX
```
alex: also run the lookup to find other tokens issued to the CI role: `vault list auth/token/accessors` then `vault token-lookup -accessor <acc>` — check for long-lived tokens.
maya: I'm going to flip on audit-log forwarding for `dev` namespace to our logging cluster and add a retention alert.
sre-bot: deploy bot: scheduled job `ci-artifact-cleaner` ran and removed object 12345 at 2025-09-01T14:12:10Z :white_check_mark:
devon: can someone take ownership of rotating KMS wrapping key for vault backups? we should consider rewrapping any backed-up ciphertexts that might have referenced the leaked token indirectly.
isabel: that's a higher blast-radius operation. let's first confirm the leak scope. if only token access was secrets below `secret/data/dev/*`, then rotate impacted secrets only. KMS rewrap is opt-in if we see evidence of backup exfil.
samir: RBAC followup: CI role should not be able to upload raw artifacts to partner buckets. we need a policy change in `ci-service` role and a repo pre-commit check to block `.env` and `*.pem` artifacts.
alex: I'll open a PR in infra: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pulls/987 to update the GCS policy and add artifact blocklist.
maya: tracker tasks:
- revoke token (devon)
- run token accessor audit (alex)
- rotate impacted secrets (isabel)
- enable per-namespace audit (maya)
- infra PR + CI blocklist (alex)
- communicate to partner + legal if we find access (devon)
ETA: EOD today for immediate revokes, next 48h for rotations.
devon: revocation done at 1768123575. confirmed via `vault token-lookup` returns "invalid token".
alex: ran accessor sweep, found 2 other transient tokens tied to same job, revoked both.
isabel: I'll start secret rotations for DB creds scoped to `dev` and post status.
maya: I'll enable audit and add alert for any vault token issuance without an associated CI run id.
samir: thanks team. can we do a quick retro on how the `.env` got packaged into artifacts? I suspect a missing `ciignore` or an old script.
devon: quick note for postmortem: partner CI copies workspace `./build/*` to bucket, we need to modify step to `tar --exclude='.env'` and add explicit allowlist.
alex: filing postmortem draft now and will ping @security-reviewers.
devon: closing thread once rotations confirmed. :lock:
